tasks.description: F633, measured on the testbed with a plain-session baseline and a blind A/B review: P5.3's text said src is set when the card ENTERS the viewport; the executor shipped `rootMargin: "200px 0px"`, said so, and renamed its test to 'once the card is near the viewport'; the phase reviewer's intentCheck answered `matches` on the basis of the executor's restatement. The blind pass also found two med defects the phase review missed. (1) The intent check QUOTES THE TASK TEXT and compares the diff and the tests against it - never against the outcome text or the test titles; a restatement whose scope differs from the task text is itself a finding, quoting both. (2) The reviewer brief puts the task text first and the executor's return last, labelled as the claim under review. (3) The drive diffs `tests.add` against the test names the return files, mechanically, and a declared case with no filed counterpart is a finding before any reviewer runs. Red-first: a fixture where the task says 'enters' and the return says 'near' with a 200px margin must answer `diverges` and quote both; a declared tests.add case missing from the return is named by the drive. (4) Measured on the testbed with the SAME model (plain Sonnet vs the plugin's Sonnet executors, blind A/B): the plugin's version alone shipped a lazy-load test that cannot fail, an e2e that drives the real server action (a key in env sends real mail), and a test-readiness race (asserting enabled state the SSR HTML already has). So the reviewer brief also asks, per declared test: can it fail on the unfixed code (the red-first block, or say it was never seen red), and does any test reach a real external service or side effect (mail, payment, network) rather than a stub - each a finding with its file:line. Faults: F633. (5) A FALSIFIER PER TEST, run by the drive at near-zero model cost (about +0.005 USD per task, research report 2026-10-12-agent-output-quality-research.md): every planned test carries a line 'must fail if <small code change>'; after the executor files, the drive applies that patch in a temporary tree (never the executor's tree) and runs the test, and a test that survives is a finding with file:line. A patch that breaks the build is could-not-run, never a kill. This REPLACES a revert-to-base check, which probe 1 measured as too weak: the plugin's P5.3 test fails on the revert yet survives the 'src set on mount' mutant, the real defect class; the plain Sonnet test kills both mount and margin_200 (artefacts danuvia-baseline/research-p53-plugin/probe-artifacts/probe1/*.log). (6) Parity in interaction states: when a task's design source names `:focus`/`:hover` rules for a form or control (as flux.css `.field input:focus` did), task synthesis writes into tests.add a design-parity case that snapshots that control's own box in its focus state (and hover where defined), not only rest, as a clipped element snapshot of that control or a computed-style assertion - a 1% threshold over a whole section hid a 2px ring (about 0.2% of the section) (2px/4px against the design's 9px, found by a live getComputedStyle probe). (7) Executor brief: scope must never push an executor into an inferior design. P6.3's plugin executor faked a 'Resend mock' by rewriting the browser response because `playwright.config.ts` was outside its scope; the plain session edited the config and ran a real mock. When the right design needs file X outside `files`, the executor files a widening request naming X and why, and does not work around it; P124's companions do not cover test infrastructure. Source: testbed monitor, 2026-10-12, at the owner's request. (8) Probe 2 (24 reviewer runs, Opus/Sonnet/Haiku, real P5.3 brief section): the brief as filed, task text first with the claim labelled, and the claim hidden each found 0/3 `diverges`; ONLY a CLAUSE-QUOTING RULE worked, 3/3 on all three models - the reviewer quotes each task clause, judges the diff against it, and a scope difference is `diverges`. (9) The tests.add-vs-filed-tests check of (3) cannot be a string diff: as one it flags 72 of 77 danuvia tasks, mostly Serbian plan text against English test titles. It matches a declared case by a verbatim title the executor must reuse, or by a clause mapping the return files; never a fuzzy string compare.

tasks.title: No report table can widen the page at any width, by construction rather than by font margin
tasks.description: Carried from P126-R2 (med, P126 phase review 2026-10-13). P126.1 made the hostile-content leg green on CI by letting the bugs table's test-gate pills wrap (`white-space:normal`), which lowers that column's narrowest width - so the page passes by margin at CI's fonts (reproduced with DejaVu in mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.56.0-jammy: +31px before, 0 after), not by an invariant: any table whose columns' min-content widths sum past the column can still widen the document above the breakpoint where `.tablewrap` starts to scroll. The structural options trade against the sticky header: (a) `.tablewrap{overflow-x:auto}` at every width - a contained scroll that can never widen the document, but `position:sticky` on thead then sticks to the wrapper, not the viewport; (b) keep the viewport-sticky header and give every non-prose column a bounded min-width plus `<wbr>` in every renderer-emitted unbroken run; (c) a JS-measured fallback that switches a table to (a) only when it overflows. Decide with the owner, implement, and add a hostile-leg case that plants a token in EVERY column kind at the narrowest unframed width on a wide-font fixture so the margin cannot be what passes it. Not a 3.2.0 regression: CI's hostile leg is green on 3.3.0.

tasks.title: Submit refuses a return whose outcome is a placeholder or whose testsAdded is empty while tests.add is not
tasks.description: F643. drive-phase.py submit checks the return's shape and then files it once per start. Two executors in P125 filed outcome.technical == outcome.descriptive == 'placeholder' with testsAdded [] (returns/P125.1/20261013T125847Z, returns/P125.2/20261013T141945Z), the second despite an explicit instruction, and the record could not be corrected. An instruction does not hold this; the filing must. Before running the helper and before writing anything, refuse: (a) outcome texts that are identical to each other, shorter than a floor stated beside the check with its reason, or a template word (placeholder, TODO, TBD, <...>); (b) testsAdded empty while the task's tests.mode is tdd or regression and tests.add is non-empty. The refusal names the field and says nothing was filed, so the agent resubmits in the same start. The check lives in the one function every return passes through (_filed_returns), not in drive-phase alone, so a reviewer return and a /audit:run filing are held to it too.

tasks.title: A concurrent writer that loses a Windows sharing race retries within its deadline instead of refusing the write
tasks.description: F615 recurred and has a twin, so this is the class, not two instances. CI run 38442950089 (ci/p125 at 125a69b8, windows-latest): test__journal_io sl4 lost a row to 'refused: [Errno 13] Permission denied ... .lock.break' (F615, first seen 2026-10-10, still unfixed), and test_panel_server hr2 had the second of two concurrent POST /api/proposal drops refused ([('first', True), ('second', False)]). The class: on Windows, opening, renaming or replacing a file another process holds is denied, and a writer that reads that denial as a refusal loses the write.
